conclusion: Allocation lifetime must be decided by the shared memory ledger; a context-local lease count cannot safely authorize free when multiple host-native contexts reference the same allocation.
decision: Count functional page tokens globally in HostGPUMemoryState and reject unmap with Busy before releasing the mapper lease whenever any competing context or dispatch pin remains.
invalidated_assumptions: One HostNativeMemoryContext can infer the complete allocation lease count.
It is safe to release a mapping lease before proving that allocation free will succeed.
observation: The cross-context test exposed token collisions and an unretryable Busy free; the accepted implementation moves token identity/counting into the shared memory state and preserves the mapping until the final release succeeds.
question_or_symptom: How can unmap remain retryable when another native context or dispatch still retains the allocation?
